header.what: What French can and cannot do with sounds, read by the checks that judge an anchor. The rules live in the engine; this file is what makes them French.
header.cannotStart: French has no /h/ phoneme at all, so hôtel is said without one; it has no /ɸ/, and no native onset for the two affricates. An anchor claiming one of these matches only on paper.
header.anchors: What an anchor of this language may be. How far a word may sit from a reading and still be heard in it, how far two anchors must sit from each other, what an unrated word is worth against a rated one, how many morae a reading may run to before no one word carries it, how common a word must be before a reader is likely to know it, and which parts of speech a story can be built on. The last is the middle of the scale the ratings use, which runs from 0 to 100 here: nothing rated the word, and that is evidence neither way.
